passages.heading: MD&A
passages.text: in our Annual Report on Form 10-K for the year ended December 31, 2024 filed with the Securities and Exchange Commission on February 18, 2025. Overview In 2025, we continued to execute our Customer First, People Led and Innovation Driven strategy, which focuses on growing in the parts of the market that value our end-to-end solutions, including healthcare, small-and medium-sized businesses ("SMBs") and International. As part of this strategy, we drove a reduction in volume from our largest customer, with a targeted reduction of 50% by June 2026 from 2024 levels. Partly as a result, we increased consolidated revenue per piece by 6.6%, and expanded SMB penetration to over 30% of total U.S. volume. In connection with this strategic execution of volume declines, we began our Network Reconfiguration and Efficiency Reimagined initiatives. These initiatives are intended to enhance the efficiency of our network through automation and operational sort consolidation in our U.S. Domestic network . From these initiatives, we delivered on our planned year-over-year cost savings of approximately $3.5 billion in 2025. See Supplemental Information - Items Affecting Comparability for additional discussion. Also in 2025, we completed the acquisitions of Frigo-Trans and Biotech & Pharma Logistics ("Frigo-Trans"), and Andlauer Healthcare Group ("AHG"). In 2025, our global healthcare portfolio generated more than $11 billion in revenue, furthering our progress towards our goal to become the number one complex healthcare logistics provider in the world. In September 2024, we completed the divestiture of our truckload brokerage services ("Coyote"), which contributed $1.6 billion of revenue in 2024 prior to its divestiture. Effective January 1, 2025, we insourced our former SurePost product, and replaced it with Ground Saver, a domestic economy service meant to complement our array of products used by our customers. This change provided us greater operational control and service quality with respect to this product. However, this insourcing pressured our operating results, as pickup and delivery costs were higher than in 2024. In December 2025, we entered into a new agreement with the United States Postal Service ("USPS") to assist with final-mile delivery for a portion of our Ground Saver and Mail Innovations volumes starting in 2026, which is expected to allow us to more cost efficiently serve our customers while maintaining our service levels. In the International market, during 2025 we implemented weekend delivery within Europe. Additionally, our new air hub in the Philippines is slated to open towards the end of 2026 and our expansion in Hong Kong is planned to open in 2028. Both gateways are expected to give us broader access and faster time in transit on the trade lanes that are growing in Asia. During 2025, we returned $6.4 billion in cash to shareholders by completing $1.0 billion of share repurchases and paying $5.4 billion in dividends. Our 2025 financial results also reflect the impact of a complex macro environment, d riven by evolving trade policies, and the significant strategic actions we are taking including revenue quality initiatives. passages.heading: Risk factors
passages.text: Our business, financial condition and results of operations are and will remain subject to numerous risks and uncertainties. You should carefully consider the following risk factors, which may have materially affected or could materially affect us, including impacting our business, financial condition, results of operations, stock price, credit rating or reputation. You should read these risk factors in conjunction with "Management’s Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations" in Item 7 and our "Financial Statements and Supplementary Data" in Item 8. These are not the only risks we face. We could also be affected by other unknown events, factors, uncertainties, or risks that we do not currently consider to be material. Additionally, the disclosures in this section reflect our beliefs and opinions as to factors that could materially and adversely affect us in the future. References to historical events are provided by way of example only, and are not intended to be a complete listing or a representation as to whether such events have occurred in the past or their likelihood of occurring in the future. Business and Operating Risks Changes or continued uncertainty in general economic conditions, in the U.S. and internationally, may adversely affect us. We conduct operations in over 200 countries and territories. Our operations are subject to national and international economic factors, as well as the local economic environments in which we operate. Changes or continued uncertainty in general economic conditions are beyond our control, and it may be difficult for us to adjust our business model. For example, we are affected by industrial production, inflation, unemployment, consumer spending, retail activity levels and international trade policies. We have been, and may in the future be, materially affected by adverse developments or uncertainty in these and other aspects of the economy. We have also been, and may in the future be, adversely impacted by changes in general economic conditions resulting from geopolitical uncertainty, tensions and/or conflicts in or arising from various countries and regions, including the European Union, Ukraine, the Russian Federation, the Middle East and the Trans-Pacific region. Changes or uncertainty in general economic conditions, or our inability to accurately forecast these changes or mitigate the impact of these conditions on our business, could materially adversely affect us. Our industry continues to rapidly evolve. We expect to continue to face significant competition, which could materially adversely affect us. Our industry continues to rapidly evolve, including demands for faster deliveries, increased visibility into shipments and development of other services. We expect to continue to face significant local, regional, national and international competition. credit_strengths.text: Gross leverage sits modestly below the sector median and comfortably inside the lower risk band, reflecting a debt load that remains proportionate to the courier and logistics earnings base despite the step-up in borrowings during the year.

Interest coverage exceeds the sector median and operating income covers gross interest several times over, so the fixed-charge burden from the senior note stack is absorbed well before earnings pressure reaches debt service.

key_risks.text: The disclosed risk factors flag dependence on industrial production, trade policy and consumer spending across more than two hundred countries; with operating margin already below the sector median, a volume or mix shock transmits quickly to earnings and coverage.

The debt note shows a large fixed-rate senior note ladder extending to mid-century plus floating-rate notes, and the maturity profile concentrates repayment after year five; refinancing that stack at higher coupons would lift interest expense and compress coverage.

debt_servicing_capacity.text: Operating cash flow covers dividends and buybacks combined, but free cash flow falls short of total shareholder distributions, so the payout is part-funded by balance-sheet capacity rather than internally generated cash alone.

Cash flow to debt sits below the sector median and below the prior year, while free cash flow to debt is also weaker than peers; the cushion to the next cash-flow risk boundary is thin, leaving limited tolerance for further EBITDA erosion.

overall_credit_view.text: The indicative financial risk profile is modest, with leverage inside the lower band and net leverage below the next threshold; the headroom is real but narrowing as debt rises faster than earnings, so the trajectory rather than the level drives our judgement.

Liquidity is adequate rather than ample: the current ratio is above one and modestly ahead of peers, but a meaningful share of current liabilities is short-dated debt, and the company is simultaneously funding network reconfiguration, healthcare acquisitions and shareholder returns.

credit_strengths.text: 毛槓桿略低於行業中位數，並穩處於較低風險區間之內，反映儘管年內借款增加，債務負擔仍與快遞及物流盈利基礎保持相稱。
利息覆蓋率超過行業中位數，且經營收入數倍於毛利息，因此高級票據層的固定費用負擔在盈利壓力觸及債務償付之前已被充分吸收。

key_risks.text: 所披露的風險因素指出，業務依賴超過二百個國家的工業生產、貿易政策及消費者支出；由於經營利潤率已低於行業中位數，銷量或組合衝擊會迅速傳導至盈利及覆蓋率。
債務附註顯示，一個大型固定利率高級票據階梯延伸至本世紀中葉，另加浮動利率票據，且到期結構將還款集中於第五年之後；以較高票息再融資該票據層將推高利息支出並壓縮覆蓋率。

debt_servicing_capacity.text: 經營現金流覆蓋股息與回購之合計，但自由現金流低於股東分派總額，故派付部分由資產負債表能力而非僅靠內部產生現金支持。
現金流對債務比率低於行業中位數且低於上年，而自由現金流對債務亦弱於同業；距下一個現金流風險界限的緩衝薄弱，對EBITDA進一步侵蝕的容忍度有限。

overall_credit_view.text: 指示性財務風險狀況為溫和，槓桿處於較低區間之內，淨槓桿低於下一個門檻；緩衝確實存在但正收窄，因債務增速快於盈利，故我們的判斷由軌跡而非水平驅動。
流動性屬足夠而非充裕：流動比率高於一且略優於同業，但流動負債中有相當比例為短期債務，而公司同時在為網絡重組、醫療保健收購及股東回報提供資金。
